paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage teaches me. Moab trusted in its works and treasures (Jeremiah 48:7), and the LORD says that trust won't hold. Moab even had its own god, Chemosh, and the LORD says Chemosh will go into exile too (Jeremiah 48:7). Whatever you stack your trust on besides the LORD, it can't carry you, and that's a LOUD lesson for anybody with a to-do list and a savings account.

Then comes the wine picture. Moab was "settled like wine on its dregs," never poured from vessel to vessel (Jeremiah 48:11). Being at ease sounds great, friend, but ease can turn into leaning on yourself without even noticing. The LORD is the one who says the days are coming, and Moab's comfort did not stop that word from coming true (Jeremiah 48:12).

And look at who is speaking. This is the King, "whose name is the LORD of Hosts" (Jeremiah 48:15), and what He says stands, town by town. So the question for you and me is simple: where does my trust sit today? I'm keeping my ovens ready and my trust on Him, and the story isn't over, because the LORD's word about Moab isn't finished.
